title: Camera permission denial and manual connection fallback
summary: Explore camera permission denial on the relationship surface and confirm that documented manual invite-code entry remains usable.
allowedActions: Reset the declared owned fixture and the target camera permission state
Open the relationship connection surface and request the documented camera permission
Deny camera access using the platform permission control and capture the resulting visible state
Enter the declared invite code manually and observe validation or pending status
Verify only the declared pending connection through the authenticated API and read-only SQL evidence
excludedExternalEffects: Real camera capture, production invite codes, customer or shared accounts
Approving or activating a connection outside the declared fixture
Device permission changes outside the owned target, provider mutations, purchases, or issue posting
Treating an unavailable permission bridge as a product failure or silently skipping the manual fallback

scenario.title: Camera denial leaves manual relationship entry available
preconditions: A fresh unlinked student fixture and a declared invite code are available
The target permission state can be reset and verified without changing a foreign device
The API/SQL identity is read-only except for the declared pending connection action
actions: Open the QR or camera entry surface
Deny the camera permission through the platform control
Inspect inline camera-unavailable guidance and the manual entry control
Submit the declared code and verify pending state through UI/API/SQL
expectedObservations: Permission denial produces recoverable guidance rather than an unrecoverable scanner
Manual invite-code entry remains enabled and localized
Pending state is consistent across the two authenticated reads and the UI
Permission transport or target blocks are retained as harness blockers
